dish: matelote au Riesling and mousseline de grenouilles (frog-leg mousseline)
address: 4 rue de Collonges au Mont d'Or, 68970 Illhaeusern, France
w: The grande dame of Alsace gastronomy on the banks of the Ill, in the Haeberlin family since 1882 and three-star from 1967 to 2018, now a two-MICHELIN-star Relais & Chateaux under Marc Haeberlin. Classic riverside dining: foie-gras terrine by the spoon, salmon souffle, the famous frog-leg mousseline.

dish: mousseline de grenouilles 'Jung' and seasonal Alsace produce
w: A MICHELIN-starred table set inside a genuine dismantled-and-rebuilt Alsatian half-timbered farmhouse in the Parc de l'Orangerie, where Eric Westermann cooks a season-driven, classically grounded cuisine. The signature frog-leg mousseline is a Strasbourg institution.

dish: creative tasting menu blending Alsace, Brittany, the US and Japan
address: 3 allee du Champ de Mars, 68000 Colmar, France
w: Colmar's two-MICHELIN-star reference, where Jean-Yves Schillinger — back home after years on the New York scene — cooks a boundary-crossing, produce-first menu in the design dining room of the L'Esquisse hotel by the Champ-de-Mars park.

dish: terroir tasting menu by Meilleur Ouvrier de France Olivier Nasti
address: 13 rue du General de Gaulle, 68240 Kaysersberg, France
w: The two-MICHELIN-star table inside the Chambard in Kaysersberg, where MOF Olivier Nasti turns Alsace terroir and game into precise, playful plates. His Bib Gourmand Winstub next door serves the traditional canon.

dish: garden-driven seasonal tasting menu (MICHELIN Green Star)
address: 5 rue de la 1ere Armee, 68340 Riquewihr, France
w: Jean-Luc Brendel's one-MICHELIN-star (plus Green Star) restaurant in a 1539 Renaissance house in medieval Riquewihr, cooking beautiful seasonal produce — much of it from his own 7,500 m2 Kobelsberg gardens of 350 species. A green-gastronomy landmark of the wine road.

dish: delicate, creative tasting menu (potato-and-truffle emulsion)
w: A two-MICHELIN-star destination in the 1920 villa René Lalique in the northern Vosges, with a Mario Botta-designed dining room and Paul Stradner's intelligent, delicate cuisine. Worth the drive for the crystal-and-cuisine setting.

dish: modern reinterpretation of Alsace classics
address: 30 rue du General de Gaulle, 67520 Marlenheim, France
w: A former posthouse at the gateway to the wine road, MICHELIN-starred since 1936 and run by the Husser family since 1930. Chef Michel Husser gives Alsace cooking a modern, refined turn around a picturesque paved courtyard.

dish: minimalist terroir tasting menu in the Maison des Tetes
w: Eric Girardin's one-MICHELIN-star (Relais & Chateaux) table inside the 1609 Maison des Tetes, whose façade carries 106 carved stone heads. An intimate 18-seat room and a spare tasting menu that showcases Alsace terroir.

dish: choucroute garnie, quenelles and jambon en croute
w: A quintessential winstub a step from the cathedral, known to locals for its quenelles, choucroute and ham baked in a pastry crust in a snug, cluttered tavern room. Listed by Gault&Millau and Petit Fute.

dish: Riesling and Gewurztraminer tasting at the Clos des Capucins
w: One of Alsace's great biodynamic estates, run by the Faller women around the walled Clos des Capucins founded by Capuchin monks in 1612. Tastings of world-class Riesling, Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer, including the Cuvee Colette and Sainte-Catherine bottlings.

dish: Riesling Clos Sainte-Hune and Cuvee Frederic Emile
w: A near-four-century Alsatian wine institution (founded 1626) in Ribeauville, benchmark for bone-dry Riesling — above all the legendary single-vineyard Clos Sainte-Hune from the Rosacker grand cru. Cellar visits and tastings on the wine route.

dish: Riesling and vendanges tardives from a house founded in 1639
address: 3 rue de la 1ere Armee, 68340 Riquewihr, France
w: A Riquewihr wine dynasty since 1639, pioneer of Alsace late-harvest (vendanges tardives) and selection de grains nobles wines. Free tastings of pure-varietal Riesling, Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Muscat in the heart of the medieval town.

dish: precise modern menu with Alsace nods, opposite the Palais Rohan
w: A one-MICHELIN-star restaurant facing the Palais Rohan (completed 1741), where a former Robuchon disciple signs delicate, precise cooking threaded with Alsatian references. Refined riverside gastronomy in the city centre.

dish: market-fresh French cuisine scattered with Asian umami notes
w: A tiny sixteen-seat one-MICHELIN-star table in Petite France, where chef Rene Fieger folds Asian notes into French, market-driven cooking. Intimate and much-praised — book well ahead.

dish: trout with choucroute and Kaefferkopf Riesling sauce
w: A one-MICHELIN-star table on the wine road at Ammerschwihr, where former Auberge de l'Ill chef Julien Binz cooks 'evolving tradition' with an Alsace accent — foie gras, Munster tortellini, trout with local Riesling sauce.

dish: three duck foie gras and mushroom fleischschnacka
w: An authentic half-timbered winstub with painted ceilings just off Petite France, where duck foie gras is king — served three ways — alongside kaseknepfle and mushroom fleischschnacka. Praised by critic Gilles Pudlowski.

dish: choucroute royale and baeckeoffe by the Ponts Couverts
w: A rustic riverside bierstub-winstub tucked between the arms of the Ill by the Ponts Couverts for nearly fifty years, serving the full canon — choucroute royale, baeckeoffe, choucroute aux trois poissons. A classic Strasbourg tavern.

dish: choucroute garnie, baeckeoffe and grumbeerekichle with bibeleskas
w: A winstub of true conviviality on quai Saint-Nicolas, run for 40-plus years by Christophe Andt and his daughter Coralie, with hearty regional classics and one of the best Alsace wine lists of its kind. A local favourite for the real thing.

dish: onion tart, veal tripe simmered in Riesling and choucroute
w: A warm, home-cooking winstub in Colmar's Little Venice run by Master Restaurateur Agostino Di Foggia, with a coveted canal-side terrace. Papi Lucien's onion tart, foie gras with Gewurztraminer, and Daniel's choucroute.

dish: choucroute au kassler and vol-au-vent under painted frescoes
w: A charming, deeply traditional winstub in Ribeauville — town of the medieval Pfifferdaj piper's festival — with old beams, colourful frescoes and hearty plates of kassler choucroute, jarret and vol-au-vent from local produce.

dish: pork in all its forms — boudin, hams, chop with morels
address: 3 place du Chateau Saint-Leon, 68420 Eguisheim, France
w: A refined Alsatian table in a 16th-century house in Eguisheim (one of France's most beautiful villages and a cradle of the wine road), MICHELIN-starred in 2004 and still cooking pork every which way — blood sausage, hams, chop with morels.

dish: bone-dry Riesling and Gewurztraminer from a 1580 estate
address: 2 rue de la Premiere Armee, 68420 Eguisheim, France
w: One of Alsace's oldest houses, in Eguisheim since 1580 and renowned for austere, food-friendly dry wines (its Comtes d'Eguisheim Riesling is a classic). Tastings at the Grand-Rue caveau; listed by the Guide Hachette des Vins.

dish: biodynamic grand-cru Riesling, Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer
w: One of the 'three greats of Alsace', a biodynamic pioneer at Turckheim whose low-yield, terroir-driven wines from grands crus Rangen and Brand are collected worldwide. Tastings by appointment at the estate.

dish: grand-cru Kirchberg tasting in historic Barr cellars
w: A family estate in Barr since 1824 with 40 hectares including prestigious Alsace grands crus, offering guided tastings and a viticulture museum in its old cellars. A dependable wine-road stop at the northern end of the route.

dish: smoked pork knuckle with potato choucroute and sandre quenelles
address: 10 place du Marche aux Choux, 67600 Selestat, France
w: A four-generation family winstub off Selestat's market square, cooking seasonal, market-led Alsatian food — smoked knuckle with potato choucroute, sandre quenelles in matelote sauce. A short-menu table that prizes freshness.

dish: Alsatian bourgeois cuisine — trout with almonds, veal kidneys with spaetzle
address: 2 rue de la Walk, 67160 Wissembourg, France
w: A riverside hotel-restaurant by an old mill on the Lauter, run by the Schmidt family for 70 years and recognised by Gault&Millau, plating Alsatian bourgeois classics — foie gras, snails, trout with almonds — ten minutes from Wissembourg's storybook old town.

dish: kougelhopf, langhopf and pain d'epices
w: A master pastry house in Munster since 1936, keeper of the classic Alsace kougelhopf (and the taller langhopf) plus pain d'epices, with a second shop in Colmar. A benchmark for the region's baking canon in the Munster valley.

dish: kougelhopf and revisited Alsatian tarts
address: 5 rue du Temple Neuf, 67000 Strasbourg, France
w: A prized pastry-chocolate house and salon de the in central Strasbourg, turning out soft kougelhopf and brioches in the morning and refined eclairs and Alsatian tarts by afternoon. Recommended by the city of Strasbourg's own guide.

dish: wood-fired tarte flambee and choucroute royale
address: 5 rue des Tailleurs de Pierre, 67000 Strasbourg, France
w: A 'winstub like the old days' by the cathedral, wood beams and private stub rooms, serving the classics — wood-fired tarte flambee, generous choucroute royale, baeckeoffe. Certified by Gault&Millau and the Collège Culinaire de France.

dish: spatzle, tarte flambee and pork knuckle on Place Benjamin Zix
w: A much-loved brasserie institution on Petite France's prettiest square, with a plane-shaded terrace over the Ill and a menu built on spatzle, salads, tarte flambee and pork knuckle. A reliable, atmospheric Petite France stop.

dish: raclette, fondue and cheese platters (Munster and 200+ cheeses)
w: A cheese-lover's temple near the cathedral — home to the world's largest cheese bell (Guinness 1989) — with 200-plus cheeses and a menu of raclette, fondue and cheese boards, a fine place to meet Alsace's Munster.

dish: specialty flat white and local Mokxa-roasted coffee
w: Strasbourg's most famous specialty coffee shop, opened in the Krutenau in 2014 and pouring locally roasted (Mokxa) coffee to expert baristas, with seasonal, partly-vegan food. The city's specialty-coffee reference.

dish: bretzel, kougelhopf and bredele
w: A Strasbourg bakery institution since 1919 on the arcaded rue des Orfevres, renowned for bretzels baked several times a day plus kougelhopf, streusel and Christmas bredele. A local go-to for the true Alsatian bretzel.
